column1: # KAN-29: a product's display name, decided once by a human and then kept -
# never recomputed from whichever chain's file happens to sort last, and
# never one of the eleven chains' names truncated at 20 characters.
# Columns: barcode, name, source, decided_at (tab-separated, UTF-8, no
# header on the data rows below - this comment block is skipped by the
# loader because it starts with '#'). `source` names where the evidence
# came from (a chain id, "pricez", "manual", ...), not a person, so it
# survives a re-review. `decided_at` is the date (YYYY-MM-DD) the row was
# accepted, not when the candidate was first seen.
# This file has room to grow: a later column (brand, size, unit, image URL,
# category) is appended after decided_at, never inserted before it, and
# existing rows are left with only four fields until they are backfilled -
# scripts/build_app_db.py's load_product_names() only unpacks the first
# four fields and ignores the rest, so old rows and old readers both keep
# working. Teaching the build to use a new column is a separate change to
# that function, not to this file's shape.
